title: Dahomey’s royal palace complex develops
summary: Successive kings built palaces at Abomey, in present-day Benin, over several centuries. The compound combined royal administration, material display and craft production within an evolving architectural setting.

claims.text: Successive kings built palaces at Abomey, in present-day Benin, over several centuries. The compound combined royal administration, material display and craft production within an evolving architectural setting.
The source’s 1625–1900 range concerns the royal succession and palace ensemble.

The palaces preserve evidence of political power through buildings and objects. Their dates mark successive construction and use, not an assertion that the kingdom or its inhabitants remained unchanged throughout this period.
